facts.fact_text: On 29 October 2003, the applicant attempted to participate in a demonstration in the form of a press conference held on Istiklal Street in the Beyoğlu district of Istanbul.
On 29 October 2003, at approximately 4.10 p.m., the applicant was arrested by police officers on Istiklal Street in the Beyoğlu district of Istanbul.
On 29 October 2003, approximately 50 to 60 other participants in the demonstration were arrested together with the applicant by police officers.
The Beyoğlu public prosecutor relied on the incident report prepared by the police officers in issuing the decision not to prosecute.
The Beyoğlu public prosecutor noted that the demonstrators had gathered illegally without obtaining permission and had disturbed public order by blocking the pedestrian zone and tramway.

The Beyoğlu public prosecutor noted that, despite warnings by the police, the demonstrators had refused to disperse, and the police had therefore been obliged to use some degree of force to disperse them and restore public order.

The Beyoğlu public prosecutor considered that the force used by the security forces had been in line with section 24 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) and had been justified in the circumstances.
In the Beyoğlu public prosecutor's opinion, the applicant's injuries were the result of a proportionate use of force which did not amount to ill-treatment or abuse of authority.

On 30 December 2004, the Istanbul Assize Court dismissed the applicant's appeal against the Beyoğlu public prosecutor's decision not to prosecute the police officers.
In a judgment dated 19 December 2006, the Beyoğlu Assize Court acquitted the applicant and her co-accused of the charges of violating the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).

The Beyoğlu Assize Court held that there was no convincing evidence indicating with sufficient certainty that the accused committed the alleged offence of breaching the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).

The Beyoğlu Assize Court held that no evidence was adduced to indicate that the accused committed the alleged offence in contravention of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) and that their action went beyond the exercise of their democratic rights.
The Beyoğlu Assize Court held that the actions of the accused were merely an exercise of their democratic rights to freedom of assembly.
